item: the Run now route answers 409 and logs a warning when the run's thread cannot start
summary: POST /api/scheduler/run-now mapped nothing when BackgroundScheduler.run_now() could not make its thread (the process or the machine out of threads): measured status 500 'internal error: can't start new thread', the only log line the global handler's, no run active afterwards, kill switch cleared. The route now catches RuntimeError around run_now(), writes one WARNING ('run now refused: the scheduler thread could not start', with the scrubbed exception) and answers 409 with the exception's words, as /start does since #1677; the Wikipedia lane is not resumed as if a run had begun. An interrupt and any other error are not mapped; a run already in flight is still a 200 with started false. run_now raises before it records anything in the scheduler's own state, so no undo is needed and runner.py is untouched. Four new tests, a run-now entry in the interrupt test and one in the log test (tests/test_failed_thread_start_routes_answer_409.py); 13 mutants killed. Stated limit (R407): what the route did before the start stays done, as after a refused /start (kill switch cleared and the crossing online noted, memory-guard and storage-guard latches reset, database-damage pauses released, and the storage-guard supervisor run_now may have started keeps running); nothing fetches without a run or a loop and the next click retries. Not observed in the field: driven by tests that inject the failure.
